newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU stability pact permits strong euro-Trichet.
newsitem.headline: EU stability pact permits strong euro-Trichet.

text.p: The European Union stability pact will allow the euro to be as solid, credible and strong as the franc, guilder or mark are now, Bank of France head Jean-Claude Trichet said in an interview with afternoon daily Le Monde.
The agreement on the stability pact at a summit in Dublin on December 13 and 14 was a decisive step in the move to monetary union, Trichet said.

"...thanks to the stability and growth pact, the euro can be as solid, as credible and as strong as the franc today, as the guilder today, as the mark today, to name three currencies which have the lowest market interest rates in the European Union," he said.
Trichet said he thought the Dublin summit had been more decisive than a summit of European leaders held in December, 1995, in Madrid,
"I think the Dublin summit was decisive, even more than the Madrid summit," Trichet said.

He said this was because the legal status of the euro had been adopted, the stability pact had been defined and the mechanism for linking European currencies outside the euro-zone to the single currency had been approved.
